paper: Delgado-Suarez EJ et al. 2021, PLoS ONE 16(5):e0243681, PMID 33951039
notes: Five genuinely open questions in 2021 Salmonella livestock AMR surveillance, grounded in what this replication tested and what it left on the table. Each has an explicit basis in either the paper's own data or the gaps our re-analysis exposed.

questions.q: Do the AMR gene profiles of cattle-derived Salmonella diverge systematically from poultry-derived Salmonella at the serovar-controlled level, or is the apparent host-species AMR divergence in the 2400-isolate NCBI Mexico cohort simply confounded by serovar composition (e.g. more Kentucky in poultry, more Anatum in cattle)?
questions.basis: C9 in REPORT.md is NOT TESTED; the paper claims cattle+poultry sources have highest MDR-genotype proportion among 2400 public Mexican Salmonella but does not stratify by serovar within source. Our S2_File.csv is loaded and available. Serovar-composition confounding is a well-known driver of apparent host-AMR patterns in Salmonella surveillance.
next_steps: Execute stratified analysis on work/public_isolates.csv: for each of the 8 focal serovars (Anatum, Reading, Typhimurium, London, Kentucky, Fresno, Muenster, Give), compare MDR-gene rate cattle vs poultry, holding serovar constant.
Compute a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test across serovar strata for host-species effect on MDR genotype.
Report the OR (cattle vs poultry) both marginally and CMH-adjusted; if the CMH OR collapses to ~1, the paper's headline is a Simpson-paradox artefact of serovar composition.

questions.q: Are plasmid-mediated colistin-resistance genes (mcr-1 through mcr-10) present in any of the 68 re-analysed isolates or the wider 2400-isolate Mexico cohort, and if so, on what plasmid backbone (IncI2, IncHI2, IncX4)?
questions.basis: REPORT.md's top-25 AMR gene table (C8) does NOT list any mcr-family gene, but AMRFinderPlus 4.2.7 does detect the full mcr-1..10 series. This is a genuine open question: 2021 was the peak of mcr-family emergence in livestock globally, and the paper predates most Latin-American mcr surveillance. The absence of mcr from our top-25 does not equal proof of absence.
next_steps: Grep the full work/all_amr_calls.tsv for '^mcr' matches across all 68 isolates and report per-serovar per-host counts.
For any mcr-positive isolate: run plasmidSPAdes or MOB-recon on the assembly to identify plasmid backbone and Inc-group.
Extend to public S2 cohort: cross-reference mcr detections against NCBI Pathogen Detection AMRFinderPlus calls for the 2400 Mexican isolates.
If mcr found, run a phenotypic colistin MIC on the source isolate (Rick has access to CLSI-panel labs).

questions.q: Can core-genome SNP-based phylogeny resolve whether the 22 Reading isolates (or the 23 Anatum isolates) represent a single Mexican outbreak clone versus multiple independent introductions, and do the AMR gene carriage patterns cluster by phylogenetic clade rather than by matrix source (LN vs GB)?
questions.basis: REPORT.md does NOT construct a phylogeny; MLST alone cannot distinguish outbreak from endemic spread within a single ST (all 22 Reading share ST-1628 or ST-7148). The ramR_M83T lineage-marker observation in REPORT.md \S5 suggests real phylogenetic structure the paper never resolved.
next_steps: Run snippy or ParSNP against a reference (e.g. S. Reading FDA-ARGOS_768 or S. Anatum FORC_034) on the per-serovar assembly sets.
Generate a core-SNP tree with iqtree2 (or a faster ML tool) and overlay LN/GB source + MDR status + ramR_M83T presence.
Compute Fisher exact within clades: does the LN-vs-GB MDR gradient hold within each major clade, or is it entirely between-clade?
If between-clade: the GB-vs-LN association is a clonal-population signal, not a matrix-contamination signal --- meaningfully different public-health implication.

questions.q: What antibiotic-use records at the source farms/slaughterhouses correspond to the AMR profiles observed, and does the temporal-spatial pattern of MDR carriage match on-farm use of tetracyclines, sulfonamides, and beta-lactams (the drug classes hit by the SGI-1 penta-cassette)?
questions.basis: REPORT.md \S1 notes samples were collected 2017-2018 in Mexico but the paper's supplementary S1_File does not include on-farm antibiotic-use metadata. This is a systemic gap in most livestock AMR-surveillance genomics work worldwide, and Mexico specifically lacks a public farm-level antibiotic-use registry.
next_steps: Request SENASICA (Mexico's national veterinary regulator) or the paper's corresponding author for de-identified on-farm antibiotic-use records tied to the collection sites.
Cross-reference the FAO INFARM / OIE ANIMUSE 2017-2018 Mexico country reports (public) for national-level tetracycline, sulfonamide, and beta-lactam use in cattle production.

If farm-level records unavailable: compute an indirect proxy via UN Comtrade veterinary-antibiotic import volumes to Mexico for 2016-2018 and test correlation with the state-level MDR-carriage rate from S2_File.
Flag this as a policy-side reproducibility gap: no genomics-driven AMR paper can be fully replicated in the epidemiological sense without linked use data.

questions.q: Do the clinical human Salmonella isolates from Mexican hospitals in the same 2017-2018 window share SNP-level identity (<20 core SNPs) with the livestock isolates in this study, providing direct One-Health evidence of farm-to-clinic transmission of the SGI-1-bearing Typhimurium lineage?
questions.basis: REPORT.md tests only livestock genomics; no human-clinical comparison. NCBI Pathogen Detection includes public human clinical Salmonella isolates from Mexico in the same window (searchable via BioSample host=Homo sapiens, geo_loc_name=Mexico). This is arguably the highest-value untested question --- it would close the One-Health loop the paper opens but does not close.
next_steps: Query NCBI Pathogen Detection browser for Salmonella Typhimurium ST-19 human clinical isolates from Mexico 2016-2019 (expected: 50-200 hits).
Fetch assemblies via datasets CLI, run snippy against a common reference (LT2 or D23580).
Construct a joint livestock+human SNP tree; identify any human isolate within 20 core SNPs of a study Typhimurium isolate (standard outbreak threshold).
For any close-match pairs: extract collection date, geographic locality, and SGI-1 status --- publish as a One-Health follow-up (this is a high-impact paper on its own if positive).
